prerequisites: Knowledge of metallic materials, metallurgy, and notions of strength of materials
Review of concepts: behavior of metallic materials, metallurgy, centers of gravity, moments of inertia, and strength of materials

learning_outcomes.text: Develop welding procedures for metallic materials.
Acquire the capacity to inspect welded joints and the manufacturing of welded elements.

syllabus_topics: Block I: Processes, Representation and Joint Design
Topic 1: Introduction to welding processes. Classification of processes (arc, resistance, solid-state). Safety and fundamental terminology.
Topic 2: Symbolic representation of welds. Symbolism according to UNE-EN ISO 2553.
Topic 3: Edge preparation and welding positions. Joint geometry according to ISO 9692. Definition of welding positions according to UNE-EN ISO 6947 (PA, PB, PC, etc.).
Topic 4: Calculation of welded joints. Design and dimensioning of butt and fillet welds. Calculation of throat thickness and stress analysis.
Block II: Metallurgy, Weldability and Cost Management
Topic 5: Welding metallurgy and thermal cycle. Study of the Heat Affected Zone (HAZ).
Topic 6: Weldability of steels. Concept of Carbon Equivalent ($CE_{IIW}$) and preheating according to UNE-EN 1011-1.
Topic 7: Welding cost management. Calculation of efficiencies, deposition rates, and labor and consumable costs.
Block III: Quality, Inspection and Qualification (Standards)

Topic 8: Defectology and Inspection. Classification of imperfections according to ISO 5817. Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) techniques: Visual Inspection (VT), Penetrant Testing (PT), Magnetic Particle Testing (MT), Ultrasonic Testing (UT), and Radiography (RT).
Topic 9: Qualification of welding procedures (WPS/WPQR). The qualification process: pWPS, Qualification Record (WPQR) and Procedure Specification (WPS) according to ISO 15614.
Topic 10: Qualification of welders. UNE-EN ISO 9606-1 standard.
Topic 11: International codes (ASME). Introduction to ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section IX: P-Numbers, F-Numbers and essential variables.
teaching_methods: Expository theory classes and classroom practices
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as (0.50 x EV-1) + (0.20 x EV-2) + (0.10 x EV-3) + (0.20 x EV-4), provided a minimum score of 4.0 out of 10 is achieved in the Final Evaluation Exam (EV-1). If the minimum for EV-1 is not met, the maximum grade recorded will be 4.0. For extraordinary calls, students can either retain continuous assessment scores and re-take the Final Exam (Conservation Pathway) or opt for a comprehensive assessment with an 80% written exam and 20% project defense (Total Evaluation Pathway), applying the same minimum conditions for the written exam. Differentiated evaluation consists of a single 100% theoretical-practical exam.
